reader.title: Broad River lynching (Spartanburg County, 1895)
bases: A1 reports two bodies, one of them bound, and a report that a local band of White Caps lynched them for miscegenation.

A1 reports the bound body of a white woman and the remains of a Black man and a report that a 'band of White Caps' killed them for miscegenation, a racial pretext; the band's size is not given, the report's source is unnamed, and A1's own headline says only 'Probably Lynched'.
The only independent report is A1; A2 is a word-for-word reprint, and no local, follow-up or Black-press account was found.

summary.text: The Broad River lynching was the reported killing of an unnamed white woman and an unnamed Black man, whose bodies were found in and beside the Broad River in Spartanburg County, South Carolina, near the North Carolina line, in August 1895.

A report described as "well-authenticated" attributed the deaths to a local band of White Caps punishing the pair for "miscegenation," though the newspaper headline called them only "Probably Lynched."
A party fishing in the Broad River brought up the body of the white woman, which was "securely bound with strong cord."
Nearby on the bank, the remains of a Black man were discovered.
The account gives no names for either victim, no date for the discovery, and no description of how the man died.
According to the report carried with the news, the two had been lynched by "a local band of White Caps for miscegenation."
The source of that report was not named, and no member of the band was identified.
No report of an inquest, an arrest or any official response appears in the coverage.
The earliest account found is a single short paragraph in the Winnsboro News and Herald of 22 August 1895, printed under the heading "Probably Lynched."
It passed on the White Cap explanation without comment and without condemning the killings.
Eight days later the Fisherman & Farmer of Edenton, North Carolina, reprinted the same paragraph under "PROBABLY LYNCHED."
No coverage of the killings was found in the Black press.

accounts.gist: A fishing party found the bound body of a white woman in Broad River and a Black man's remains on the bank; a 'well-authenticated report' attributed the killings to White Caps punishing 'miscegenation'.

framing.detail: Headed 'Probably Lynched'; reports the White Cap explanation as a 'well-authenticated report' without comment or condemnation.
